issues.issue: Panel (b) is the headline, but the gap bracket is a nearly invisible hairline box at 40% (1.4 x-units wide, lavender on white, partly overdrawn by the bands). A reader cannot see how much of the gap the filter closes, so the message 'wins back much of the accuracy' is only readable by eye-balling three lines.
issues.fix: Make the gap explicit: draw a wider, more saturated #F1EEF7 band with a #B6ACD1 edge (or a bracket just right of the 40% points) from noisy logistic regression to the clean level, and add a short label such as 'gap' or the points recovered (e.g. 'filter recovers X of Y points', value from a recipe with \src). Do the same on breast cancer, where the filter sits inside the bracket only by a few points.

issues.issue: Panel (c) is cramped and its two sub-axes are labeled inconsistently: one has a two-line small-font title ('filter minus logistic reg.', 6.5 pt) and the other the single word 'dropped'; two rotated y labels sit next to each other; rotated x tick labels eat the bottom third. At a glance it is unclear that the left bars are a cost and the right bars a different quantity.
issues.fix: Give both sub-axes titles in the same font size and the same style ('accuracy change' / 'samples dropped'), shorten the y labels ('points', '% dropped'), and replace the rotated tick labels by short horizontal ones ('digits', 'breast c.') or a shared label under the pair. Widen the panel slightly (e.g. 28/44/28) and add more wspace between the two sub-axes.

issues.issue: Vertical space is wasted and the baselines of the panels do not line up: all panels end near 0.3 of the height with a large empty band beneath, while panel (a) has its group labels placed lower than (b)'s x label and (c)'s rotated ticks. The panels look like three separate figures.
issues.fix: Reduce the aspect (e.g. 0.36) or lower the bottom margin, align x-label baselines across (a), (b), (c), and align the top of the axes so the (b) subplot titles and (c) titles sit on one line.

issues.issue: Panel (a) legend entry 'half of drops' is cryptic for a dashed line that sits behind the bars, and 'precision (ours)' tags a metric as ours while recall is not, which reads oddly. The y axis says 'Share (%)' without saying of what.
issues.fix: Label the line '50%' on the axis or label 'chance: half of drops flipped' next to the line; drop '(ours)' from the precision entry (the purple already codes the method); name the metrics in the legend with their meaning, e.g. 'precision: drops that are flips' and 'recall: flips that are dropped'.

issues.issue: Logistic regression is blue, not the specified muted teal, and the MLP line and filter bands overlap heavily on breast cancer at 20-40% noise (wide sd bands), making the filter-vs-logreg comparison muddy there.
issues.fix: Use a distinctly teal hue for logistic regression consistent with the paper's other figures, and lower band alpha to about 0.10 or switch to error bars at the 20% and 40% points for breast cancer so the filter line stays clear.

issues.issue: Honesty: panel (b) y axes are truncated and differ between digits (60s-100) and breast cancer, and (c) digits bar is negative with an interval from about -0.9 to +0.3. The caption does not mention the truncated axes, and says the interval 'includes zero' for (c) though breast cancer only touches zero in the notes.
issues.fix: Add to the caption that the y axes in (b) do not start at zero and differ between datasets; state 'includes or touches zero' for (c); mention that the filter's clean-label mean is slightly below logistic regression on both datasets.

strengths: Clean three-panel structure with lowercase panel letters, no titles inside the plots beyond dataset names, and legends above the axes, never over data.
The accent is used consistently: the filter is purple and thicker in (b), precision is purple in (a), and the cost bars in (c) are purple, so our method is easy to find.
The MLP collapse and the filter's flatter curve are visible immediately in (b), and the gray clean-label line gives a clear target.
Panel (a) shows precision with sd error bars and a 50% reference, and panel (c) shows an honest paired interval that crosses zero rather than hiding the small negative mean.
